title: Sheaf dg algebras, right modules and normalized scalar systems on a ringed site
statement:
Fix a site $(C,J)$ small in the coefficient universe as in [def-weil-size-convention] and a sheaf $O$ of commutative rings. In the category of $O$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], use integer cochain complexes and their direct-sum total tensor with Koszul differential [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], built from the sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A sheaf dg algebra $A$ is a monoid object in this monoidal category. A right dg $A$-module is a left module object over $A$ in the reversed tensor category; its underlying complex and action are the standard forgetful functor and module action. Restriction along a monoid morphism $\varphi:A\to B$ is precomposition of the action. Let $W_A$ be the maps inducing isomorphisms on every cohomology sheaf of the underlying complex, and $D(A)=\operatorname{Mod}_{dg}(A)[W_A^{-1}]$, the formal-inverse localization, with canonical functor $Q_A$. This model is equivalent to first quotienting by dg homotopy and then localizing, since cylinders invert homotopy equivalences.

A shift comparison identifies the underlying complex with the usual $M[n]$ and the unchanged right action. A cone comparison identifies the underlying complex with the usual signed cochain mapping cone, its action with the componentwise action on $N\oplus M[1]$, and its maps with inclusion and the standard signed connecting map. A standard derived structure is a triangulated structure [def-weil-triangulated-category] on this fixed localization, with shift comparisons natural in module maps, every dg shift and cone present, and distinguished triangles exactly the isomorphic images of these cone triangles.

For $\varphi:A\to B$, a balanced tensor presentation of $M\otimes_A B$ is a right $B$-module $T$, a balanced right-$B$-linear chain map $M\otimes_O B\to T$, universal for such maps to every right $B$-module. Balanced means $(ma)\otimes b=m\otimes\varphi(a)b$; the differential is inherited from the ordinary total tensor. An ordinary scalar-extension presentation is a functor of these representing objects and their natural universal maps, with the restriction adjunction whose unit is $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ and counit is $n\otimes b\mapsto nb$.

A scalar model, conditional on standard derived structures, consists of this ordinary extension, its total left derived functor with comparison $LQ_A\to Q_BF$ satisfying the right Kan universal property, and the restriction functor factored through $Q_B$ by a natural isomorphism. Both derived functors commute with shift and are exact; the extension is left adjoint to restriction. Its counit at $Q_BN$ is the localization comparison followed by the ordinary action counit (transported by the restriction factorization), and the inverse Hom transpose is $f\mapsto L(f)\,;\epsilon_N$. A scalar system packages standard source and target structures with such a model, without asserting that it exists. The signed opposite algebra uses the Koszul braiding, and left modules are right modules over this opposite; opposite homomorphisms are obtained by functoriality. All constructions in this paragraph are definitions of data, not existence assertions.
